report.executive_summary: Autonomous threat hunt completed. Multiple ATT&CK techniques confirmed.

findings.title: Brute Force Attack on Administrator Account
findings.description: Systematic brute force attack targeting the Administrator account from source IP 192.168.1.105. Attack involved 15 failed logon attempts over approximately 4 minutes (02:30:03 to 02:34:27) using LogonType 3 (network logon), indicating SMB-based credential attack. Attack succeeded at 02:36:44, resulting in successful compromise of Administrator credentials. All failed attempts cite "Unknown user name or bad password" as failure reason.
evidence: EventID=4625 | TargetUserName=Administrator | TargetDomainName=CORP | IpAddress=192.168.1.105 | Multiple events from 02:30:03-02:34:27
EventID=4624 | Time=2024-06-15T02:36:44 | TargetUserName=Administrator | IpAddress=192.168.1.105 | Successful logon post-brute force
15 failed logon attempts (4625) with consistent targeting and error pattern

findings.title: Lateral Movement via SMB Network Connections
findings.description: Post-compromise, attacker executed lateral movement attempts to other systems using SMB protocol. Network connections established to 192.168.1.115:445 and 192.168.1.110:445. Command executed to access C$ administrative share on 192.168.1.110 using credentials 'Administrator:Lab123!'. This indicates successful reconnaissance followed by active lateral movement exploitation.
evidence: Sysmon EventID=3 | Time=2024-06-15T03:01:37 | net.exe connecting to 192.168.1.115:445 TCP
Sysmon EventID=3 | Time=2024-06-15T03:03:47 | net.exe connecting to 192.168.1.110:445 TCP
EventID=4688 | Time=2024-06-15T03:01:45 | net use \\192.168.1.110\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123!

findings.title: PowerShell Abuse for Post-Exploitation Command Execution
PowerShell Abuse for Post-Exploitation Command Execution
findings.description: Attacker utilized PowerShell extensively for post-exploitation activities including execution of AtomicRedTeam testing framework with execution bypass, system reconnaissance, credential enumeration, and Windows Defender disablement. Commands executed via powershell.exe include import of Atomic Red Team modules, querying lsass process, and SetMpPreference cmdlets to disable realtime monitoring.
evidence: EventID=4688 | powershell.exe -exec bypass -c "Import-Module C:\AtomicRedTeam\invoke-atomicredteam\Invoke-Atom"
EventID=4688 | Time=2024-06-15T02:46:20 | powershell.exe -c "Get-Process | Where-Object {$_.Name -eq 'lsass'}"
EventID=4688 | Time=2024-06-15T02:55:58 | powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true
Multiple Sysmon EventID=1 process creation events for ipconfig.exe, hostname.exe, whoami.exe, systeminfo.exe via PowerShell parent

findings.title: System Discovery and Reconnaissance Activities
findings.description: Attacker executed comprehensive system discovery and reconnaissance commands to enumerate system configuration, users, processes, and network information. Commands executed include systeminfo, hostname, whoami /all, ipconfig /all, net user, and process enumeration targeting lsass.exe. All reconnaissance commands were executed through PowerShell, indicating attacker's information gathering phase post-compromise.
evidence: Sysmon EventID=1 | Time=2024-06-15T02:44:40 | systeminfo command via PowerShell
Sysmon EventID=1 | Time=2024-06-15T02:42:44 | hostname command via PowerShell
Sysmon EventID=1 | Time=2024-06-15T02:45:22 | whoami /all command via PowerShell
Sysmon EventID=1 | Time=2024-06-15T02:45:26 | ipconfig /all command via PowerShell
Sysmon EventID=1 | Time=2024-06-15T02:46:13 | net user enumeration via PowerShell

findings.title: Windows Defender Disablement and Security Control Bypass
findings.description: Attacker disabled Windows Defender and other security controls to evade detection. Multiple PowerShell commands executed Set-MpPreference to disable realtime monitoring and behavioral monitoring. Registry modification directly set HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\DisableAntiSpyware to disable antispyware protection. These actions indicate deliberate defense evasion post-compromise to maintain persistence.
evidence: EventID=4688 | Time=2024-06-15T02:44:54 | powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true
EventID=4688 | Time=2024-06-15T02:55:58 | powershell.exe Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true
Sysmon EventID=13 | Time=2024-06-15T02:56:28 | Registry modification HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware via powershell.exe

findings.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task and Registry Modifications
findings.description: Attacker established persistence mechanisms through scheduled task creation and registry modifications. A scheduled task named "\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WindowsUpdate\\UpdateCheck" was created with PowerShell execution payload (IEX obfuscated command). Additionally, registry Run key was modified at HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate pointing to attacker payload. These mechanisms ensure malware execution upon system restart.
evidence: EventID=4698 | Time=2024-06-15T02:53:15 | TaskName=\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\UpdateCheck | SubjectUserName=Administrator | TaskContent contains PowerShell with IEX
Sysmon EventID=13 | Time=2024-06-15T03:06:20 | Registry SetValue HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\WindowsUpdate via reg.exe

findings.title: Security Event Log Clearing and Cover-Up Activity
findings.description: Attacker cleared the Windows Security event log at 03:15:04 on 2024-06-15 to cover tracks and remove evidence of malicious activities. Event ID 1102 indicates the audit log was cleared by Administrator user. This represents final stage of attack where attacker deliberately attempted to remove forensic evidence of the brute force attack, lateral movement, reconnaissance, and persistence mechanisms established during the compromise.
evidence: EventID=1102 | Time=2024-06-15T03:15:04 | Host=WORKSTATION-01 | SubjectUserName=Administrator | SubjectDomainName=CORP | Description=The audit log was cleared

## Summary of Investigation Results:

Based on comprehensive analysis of the Windows security logs, I've identified **CONFIRMED MALICIOUS ACTIVITY** across all five hypotheses. Here are the detailed findings:

### **HYPOTHESIS 1: Brute Force/Password Guessing (T1110.001) - CONFIRMED**
- **15 failed logon attempts** targeting Administrator account from source IP 192.168.1.105
- All failures due to "Unknown user name or bad password" 
- LogonType=3 indicates network-based SMB authentication attacks
- Attacks occurred over 4 minutes (02:30:03 - 02:34:27)
- **1 successful logon** at 02:36:44 from same source IP post-brute force attempt

### **HYPOTHESIS 2: Lateral Movement via SMB (T1021.002) - CONFIRMED**
- Network connection to 192.168.1.115:445 (SMB) at 03:01:37
- Network connection to 192.168.1.110:445 (SMB) at 03:03:47
- Command execution: `net use \\192.168.1.110\C$ /user:Administrator Lab123!` at 03:01:45
- Clear evidence of lateral movement attempts to other hosts

### **HYPOTHESIS 3: PowerShell Command Execution (T1059.001) - CONFIRMED**
- Multiple PowerShell processes used for post-exploitation activities
- Command: `powershell.exe -exec bypass -c "Import-Module C:\\AtomicRedTeam\\invoke-atomicredteam\\Invoke-Atom"` (apparent red team activity)
- Commands to disable Windows Defender: `Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $true -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $true`
- Reconnaissance commands executed via PowerShell (ipconfig, hostname, whoami, systeminfo, net user)

### **HYPOTHESIS 4: System Discovery/Reconnaissance (T1082) - CONFIRMED**
- Multiple system discovery commands executed via PowerShell:
  - systeminfo
  - hostname  
  - whoami /all
  - ipconfig /all
  - net user
  - Get-Process targeting lsass.exe

### **HYPOTHESIS 5: Defense Evasion (T1562.001) - CONFIRMED**
- Windows Defender disabled via PowerShell Set-MpPreference commands
- Registry modification: `HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\DisableAntiSpyware`
- Persistence mechanism: Registry Run key modified with `HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\WindowsUpdate`
- Scheduled task created: `\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\UpdateCheck` with PowerShell execution
- **Event log clearing** at 03:15:04 - Event ID 1102 indicates audit log was cleared

Now I'll confirm all findings:
iteration_log.action: confirm_finding({"title": "Brute Force Attack on Administrator Account", "description": "Systematic brute force attack targeting the Administrator account from source)
iteration_log.observation: Finding #1 confirmed and added to report: Brute Force Attack on Administrator Account
